title: Compiled Python bytecode (.pyc) committed to the repo
evidence:
diff --git a/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f807a4d
Binary files /dev/null and b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc differ
detail: A CPython 3.13 cache artifact is added as a tracked binary file. It is machine-generated, version-pinned noise that will churn on every interpreter change; the same PR gitignores .pp-settings.bin but not __pycache__.
recommended_fix: Remove the .pyc from the index and add `__pycache__/` (or *.pyc) to .gitignore.

title: derive_a11y_palettes.py ships unused helpers (scale_lum, mix, lum)
detail: derive() uses only hand-set anchor tuples; scale_lum, mix, and lum (called solely inside scale_lum) are never invoked anywhere in the script — dead code contradicting the 'derivation by numeric search' docstring.
recommended_fix: Delete scale_lum/mix/lum (and lum's remaining use), or wire the search step the docstring describes.

title: verify() takes an unused tune parameter
detail: tune=True is accepted and never read; both call sites pass the default. A leftover from the removed auto-nudging the docstring disclaims.
recommended_fix: Drop the tune parameter (and the 'tune' implication) or implement it.

title: CI gate 2's label still says 'Core unit tests' but the command now runs five test suites with a 3x repeat
evidence:
GATES=(
  "Purity + grep gates (ODN-1)|tools/lint.sh"
  "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|mkdir -p bin && odin test core && for i in 1 2 3; do odin test app -out:bin/app-test || exit 1; done && odin test app/render -out:bin/render-test && odin test app/audio -out:bin/audio-test && odin test harness -out:bin/harness-test"
detail: The gate's human-readable name no longer matches its body: it now runs app, render, audio, and harness suites plus a 3x app repeat — mislabeled in any CI report or failure output.
recommended_fix: Rename the gate label to cover all five suites (e.g. 'Unit tests (core + app + render + audio + harness, 3x app)').

title: palcheck's map-pair threshold depends on pair-member ORDER (pr[0] only)
detail: The 40-vs-48 threshold picks the map tier by inspecting only pr[0]; a future pair appended as [signal, water] or with canvas first would silently get the laxer 40 gate. The Python twin keys on an explicit label instead.
recommended_fix: Tag each pair with its threshold (like pair_list's (label, a, b, t) tuples) instead of sniffing pr[0].
